correctness.rationale: For 2≤q≤(p−1)/2, mq=(2q−1)p+(p−q)<p², each md has larger units digit, so one borrow. At q0=(p+1)/2, mq0=p²+(p−1)/2 forces two borrows for every d<q0; no third possible. For q=q0+j, 1≤j≤(p−1)/2, units borrow for every d, while d=q0 yields exactly one carry in the complementary addition (next digit 2j≤p−1). At q=p+1, d=q0 has no borrow by Lucas. All cases include p=3 boundaries. Independent valuation via Legendre factorial sums was compared against the exact formula for all 2274 odd-prime/multiplier cells with p≤149; universal claim rests on Kummer case proof. General Fairfax-Ball ceiling r_p(2p−1)=2 supplies maximality globally.
